statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ front-month trades near 29,618 (+0.18%) inside the 29,530.50-29,682.50 band, roughly 0.51% wide, that has now contained about thirteen hours of trade with the session high still unretested. Tail holds at 5 because the price path remains contained and two-way and because the oil impulse has flattened: Brent is $96.66 (+0.40%) and WTI $91.61 (+0.15%), both consolidating rather than extending after last week's 9.3% and 9.7% gains. Stress stays at 55 on the standing Iran and Hormuz premium, a live September Fed hike debate and the PPI/CPI stack later this week. US cash equity and Treasury markets are closed for Labor Day, CME equity index futures halt at 17:00 UTC and restart at 22:00 UTC, and the flagged 15:00-17:00 UTC window covers the European cash close running into that halt.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD, and Tail remains far below the block threshold in every hour of this outlook. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European cash close into the shortened Labor Day futures halt, and secondarily at the 22:00 UTC restart that opens the Tuesday trade date after five closed hours. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The elevated Stress reading describes a difficult but recoverable environment and does not by itself change the mapped state.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a thirteen-hour band through the Labor Day session as oil consolidates near $96.65 Brent and US cash markets stay shut
body:
The price path remains the strongest evidence this hour and it continues to argue for a low tail value. The band from 29,530.50 to 29,682.50, about 0.51% wide, has now contained roughly thirteen hours of trade. The session high was made, rejected and has still not been retested; NQ is near 29,618, up 0.18%, and has drifted back towards the middle of the band from the 29,637 area seen an hour ago. Containment with working retracements is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency that overwhelms a mean-reversion approach.

Oil is elevated but no longer impulsive. Brent is $96.66, up 0.40% on the day and still below the $97.58 peak reached in the early European hours, while WTI is $91.61, up 0.15%. Last week Brent gained about 9.3% and WTI about 9.7% on renewed US-Iran fighting. This session the geopolitical premium is holding rather than compounding. The US struck three Iranian oil tankers over the weekend in retaliation for ballistic missile attacks on US Navy warships, and Tehran has threatened a new restricted maritime zone in the Persian Gulf, but the US Energy Secretary said millions of barrels were still moving through the Strait of Hormuz. A premium that stabilises intraday raises Stress without supplying a Tail amplifier.

Cross-asset alignment is absent, which is itself informative. Asia-Pacific closed sharply higher, with the Nikkei 225 up 2.12% and the Kospi up 4.61% on semiconductor strength including Samsung at +5.68% and SK Hynix at +8.26%, while Europe is mixed: the STOXX 600 near -0.1%, the DAX -0.14%, the FTSE 100 broadly flat and the CAC 40 and FTSE MIB each about +0.1%. VIX last printed 15.05 before the Cboe holiday closure. US Treasury cash is shut, so the H.15 curve as of 3 September, with the 2-year at 4.34%, the 10-year at 4.77% and the 30-year at 5.25%, is the latest available reference and cannot move today. Divergence of this kind normally lifts uncertainty rather than tail risk.

The macro backdrop is what keeps Stress at 55. August payrolls came in at 162,000 with unemployment steady at 4.1%, and following Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole address on 28 August, implied odds of a 25bp hike at the 15-16 September FOMC have run at roughly 60-68%. PPI lands Thursday, the ECB decides the same morning at 12:15 UTC, and CPI follows on Friday. Under the calibration used here an unresolved catalyst stack of this kind maps to Stress and to Confidence, not to Tail, until an observed price path establishes retracement failure.

Structure of the day matters more than usual. NYSE, Nasdaq and the US bond market are closed for Labor Day, CME equity index futures halt at 17:00 UTC and restart at 22:00 UTC for the Tuesday trade date. The flagged 15:00-17:00 UTC window covers the European cash close running into that halt, when depth thins from both venues at once and a headline impulse would be poorly absorbed. The 22:00 UTC restart carries a second, narrower conditional risk because five closed hours concentrate any accumulated news into a single repricing; the equivalent restart on 6 September proved orderly. Neither is an observed condition, both are conditional allowances, and every hour in this outlook remains inside the low tail band.

The shared Finviz cross-asset context file was last collected at 06:39 UTC and is therefore outside the 90-minute freshness limit, so this assessment rests on independently fetched primary sources rather than that context.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available; the 21:00 UTC hour on 6 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable with null fields. Tail held a flat 5 through the closed-venue Sunday session, mapping to EA_ON and green in every available hour, stepped to 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart to carry reopen-gap risk, eased back to 5 once that restart proved orderly, lifted to 7 as the overnight high extended, and settled at 6 and then 5 as that high was retraced and left unretested. Stress ranged from 54 to 60, peaking at 60 into the Sunday close before easing into the low-to-mid fifties across the Asian and European hours. Confidence sat between 84 and 86 throughout. The dominant mode was normal in every available hour, and no hour in the window produced observed persistent one-way structure.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover the rest of the European morning and a holiday afternoon traded against closed US cash equity and Treasury markets, a shortened futures session that halts at 17:00 UTC, five closed hours, the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date, and the Tuesday Asian session into the European cash open. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band in every hour: 5 for the current hour and the next, 6 across the late European morning and the holiday afternoon where thinned depth meets no US cash backstop, 8 in the flagged 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European close into the halt, 5 through the five closed hours where no price path can form, 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart for concentrated gap repricing, and 6 to 7 across the Tuesday Asian session and the European cash open. Stress runs from 50 during the halt to 58 in the flagged window, and Confidence decays from 85 to 72 with horizon. Every hour maps to EA_ON and green, and the dominant mode stays normal throughout because no observed evidence supports a directional or event-driven label.
